proposal_record.raw:
{
  "diagnosis": "The agent repeatedly fails in three recurring ways: (1) it substitutes a plausible or brand-name-linked medicine for the specific generic/agent-supported option, or rejects a correct option because of an unstated concern rather than dialogue evidence; (2) it treats inferred, remembered, or prior-answer context as if it were a patient fact, especially for contraindications, interactions, or comorbidities; and (3) it does not reliably retrieve exact patient excerpts that disambiguate which medicine is appropriate for the stated condition. This indicates that option selection is over-relying on general drug-category plausibility instead of mapping the stated diagnosis or symptom pattern to the single best-supported named option, and safety checks are inventing or importing facts not present in the dialogue.",
  "skills": [
    {
      "id": "exact_condition_option_match",
      "text": "When choosing among medicines, first identify the stated condition or syndrome from the dialogue and then require the chosen option to have a direct indication for that exact condition or its core symptom. Prefer the option with the clearest condition-specific indication over a broader, plausible, or off-target option. Do not select based only on drug-category similarity or brand familiarity."
    },
    {
      "id": "generic_over_brand_priority",
      "text": "When two options refer to the same active ingredient or one is a brand name and the other is its generic, treat them as equivalent medicines; if the question asks for the medicine and both are otherwise correct, prefer the generic or the option explicitly presented as the medicine rather than the brand-only label. This skill applies only when equivalence is stated or textually evident; do not invent equivalence."
    },
    {
      "id": "no_invented_interaction_or_contraindication",
      "text": "Do not reject or downrank a correct option because of a possible interaction, contraindication, or comorbidity that is not explicitly stated in the dialogue. Safety exclusions require a stated fact or a directly retrievable patient excerpt. If no contraindication is documented, do not treat the absence of a contraindication statement as a contraindication."
    },
    {
      "id": "exact_excerpt_before_selection",
      "text": "Before final option selection, retrieve the shortest exact dialogue excerpts that state the patient's condition, current medicines, prior failed therapy, and any safety-relevant facts. Use only those excerpts as the factual basis. If an option's indication is supported by the stated condition and no explicit dialogue fact rules it out, select it rather than an alternative supported only by general reasoning."
    },
    {
      "id": "prefer_first_line_over_alternative_unless_contraindicated",
      "text": "When multiple options could be used for the stated condition, prefer the option that is the standard first-line or best-supported therapy for that exact condition. Do not substitute a less-established alternative merely because it is also used in the same disease area, unless the dialogue explicitly states a contraindication, intolerance, or prior failure of the preferred option."
    }
  ],
  "focus_terms": [
    "diagnosed with",
    "taking",
    "currently taking",
    "has been taking",
    "history of",
    "suspected of having",
    "initial diagnosis",
    "my initial diagnosis is",
    "elevated triglycerides",
    "LDL cholesterol",
    "trigeminal neuralgia",
    "urothelial carcinoma",
    "multiple sclerosis",
    "muscle spasms",
    "depression with anxiety",
    "lichen simplex chronicus",
    "Asperger's",
    "autism spectrum",
    "Zollinger-Ellison syndrome",
    "osteoporosis",
    "low bone mineral density",
    "no contraindication",
    "not indicated"
  ],
  "modules": {
    "patient_evidence": "Extract the stated diagnosis or syndrome, current medicines, prior treatments and responses, and any explicitly stated safety facts using exact dialogue excerpts. Do not infer missing facts such as interactions, contraindications, or comorbidities from general medical knowledge or from the options themselves.",
    "safety_check": "Check only for contraindications and interactions that are explicitly stated in the dialogue. If no safety-relevant fact is documented, do not create one and do not exclude an option solely because a hypothetical interaction could exist. Treat absence of a stated contraindication as no documented contraindication, while still applying basic label logic only where the dialogue directly supports it.",
    "option_selection": "Match the option to the exact stated condition or syndrome, preferring the most condition-specific and best-supported therapy. When a brand and generic represent the same medicine, prefer the generic or the option presented as the medicine if equivalence is explicitly or textually evident. Do not choose a less-specific plausible option when a condition-specific option is available and not explicitly ruled out by dialogue facts."
  }
}
